requirement_paraphrase: Basic safety publication on what to consider when E/E/PE systems perform safety functions; guides sector standards and safety-system development.

Covers E/E/PE hardware design and manufacture (not software), turning Part 1 requirements into design requirements, including installation, commissioning and final safety validation; measures graded against safety integrity level.

Software requirements: safety lifecycle activities graded by required systematic capability, support tool requirements, information to integrators, and requirements for organisations modifying safety software.

instrument: Burton et al., ML safety case in highly automated driving
requirement_paraphrase: Argues ML performance evidence has limits and needs explicit confidence arguments covering training data, test-data sufficiency and whether results reflect the claim; proposes combining several evidence kinds.
applies_to: ML perception in automated driving (transferable idea)

instrument: Vardal et al. - Learning Run-time Safety Monitors for ML Components
requirement_paraphrase: Builds a monitor from perturbation experiments (haze, blur) that predicts safety level of ML output; reports 92% monitor accuracy on a simple traffic-sign case; authors list limitations (uniform perturbations, single-shot inputs).

instrument: UK MoD Def Stan 00-056 via MOD ASEMS guidance SMP12
requirement_paraphrase: Safety case is a structured argument supported by evidence; minimum contents include requirements met, validity of requirements, SMS implemented as defined, competent key staff, and legal/standards compliance. Argument should be single and coherent.
applies_to: UK MOD acquisition programmes (binding force arises through MOD contracts, not verified here)

instrument: UNECE WP.29 ADS regulation (reported as GTR No. 26 / UN Regulation No. 185; doc ECE-TRANS-WP.29-2026-139e)
clause_or_section_seen: As reported by secondary sources (clause numbers not seen)
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers must reportedly submit a safety case showing the ADS presents no unreasonable risk (at least as safe as a competent and careful human driver) and maintain an audited lifecycle-wide SMS; compliance is reportedly shown via simulation, closed-track and real-world validation.
applies_to: L3-L5 ADS vehicles in jurisdictions applying the UN instrument

requirement_paraphrase: Reported to require ongoing post-deployment monitoring and reporting; a Data Storage System for Automated Driving; prompt reporting of critical events (collisions, operation outside ODD, cybersecurity incidents, emergency manoeuvres, unauthorized modifications) with follow-up reports within 30 days where required; annual safety-performance data.
Reported to bar real-time in-vehicle self-learning that changes driving behaviour, and to require a software update process, remote termination capability and cybersecurity controls.

instrument: BSI PAS 1883 ODD taxonomy for an ADS
status_note: Publicly Available Specification, not a British Standard; to be withdrawn when published as a BS; reviewed at <=2-year intervals
requirement_paraphrase: Gives a minimum hierarchical ODD taxonomy (scenery, environmental conditions, dynamic elements). Environmental attributes include wind, rainfall, snowfall, particulates (incl. airborne dust and sand) and illumination. Excludes test procedures and monitoring requirements for ODD attributes.

instrument: BSI PAS 1883 ODD taxonomy for an ADS
requirement_paraphrase: Temperature is only an optional extra weather attribute, not a defined attribute; glare is mentioned only as a detrimental effect in the illumination text, though sun elevation and position are illumination attributes (cl. 5.3.3); the term GNSS is not used - positioning is covered as Galileo/GLONASS/GPS under connectivity (5.3.4) with signal strength/interference as optional sub-attributes, and loss of positioning signal appears as an interference zone under scenery zones (5.2.2(e)).

requirement_paraphrase: SORA is a recommended methodology to establish confidence that a specific operation can be conducted safely: ConOps evaluation, categorisation into six SAIL levels, then recommended operational safety objectives per SAIL.

requirement_paraphrase: Robustness = lower of integrity and assurance level. Low assurance: applicant declares; medium: applicant supplies evidence (testing/operational data); high: verified by a competent third party. Three robustness levels (low, medium, high).

requirement_paraphrase: Documentation of the operation: maps and data for ground/air risk, flight profiles incl. nominal, contingency and emergency phases, mitigations, contingency volume and ground risk buffer and how they were determined.

status_note: Release, edition date 13.05.2024; JARUS publications page lists v2.5 as newest; copy read from Czech CAA mirror, not jarus-rpas.org
requirement_paraphrase: Intrinsic GRC from max UA characteristic dimension/speed and highest population density in the footprint (operational volume plus ground risk buffer). UA of 250 g or less and 25 m/s or less gets iGRC 1; combinations without an iGRC are outside SORA (certified category). Guidance (4.2.4) says the operational volume should account for navigation solution accuracy, flight technical error, path definition (map) error and latencies.

status_note: Release, edition date 13.05.2024; JARUS publications page lists v2.5 as newest; copy read from Czech CAA mirror, not jarus-rpas.org
requirement_paraphrase: Optional ground-risk mitigations lower the GRC: M1(A) sheltering -1 (low) / -2 (medium); M1(B) operational restrictions -1 (medium) / -2 (high); M1(C) ground observation -1 (low); M2 impact reduction -1 (medium) / -2 (high). Final GRC above 7 is out of SORA scope (certified category).
